pattern.crimePattern: miner whose late husband was cheated kills the gold buyer with a rigged scale and hides the body in a shaft collapse
pattern.notes: Fictional buyer, miners' group and shaft. Rigged scales are a known grievance in artisanal mining; the miners themselves are shown as hard-working and wronged, not stigmatised. Mercury is named only as a decoy method; no handling detail.

ob.text: Miners at Macalder report that shaft 7 partly collapsed at about 07:30. At 09:00 they dug out a gold buyer, Rosebella Ogutu (45), at the bottom under fallen earth and timber. Recorded as a mining accident.

facts.text: Shaft 7 partly collapsed at about 07:30. At 09:00 miners dug out gold buyer Rosebella Ogutu at the bottom. Recorded as a mining accident.
Rosebella was at the bottom of shaft 7 under fallen earth and timber, with one head wound.
Under the pan of Rosebella's digital scale, a small magnet is glued in place.
A certified 1-gram reference weight in a plastic case, with a school's label.
On Rosebella's scale the certified 1 g weight reads 0.90 g. With the magnet removed, it reads 1.00 g. Every sale was weighed about 10% light.
Rosebella's ledger: Robi's husband sold to her for six years, Robi for three. Every sale was paid, short but paid.
Boke: at about 05:50, from the next shaft, she heard two women arguing at shaft 7: "You've cheated us for years — my husband too!" Then quiet.
Boke was down her own shaft hauling, in view of her partner, from 05:30.
Boke: at 06:30 the miners queued at Rosebella's kiosk to sell. It never opened, for the first time in twelve years.
Pond log: "R. Wambura — 06:40".
Nyakerario: Robi arrived at about 06:40, out of breath. She left her pan "to go and check something" at about 07:15 and came back at 07:40, shaking.
Nyakerario was at the ponds with the log from 05:30.
Nyakerario: there has never been a dispute over places at the ponds. "Everyone washes where she washes."
Shaft 7's props are rotten through, except one sound prop with fresh stone-strike marks at its base, now lying across the mouth.
A band of dark red clay runs round shaft 7's mouth and nowhere else in the field.
Shaft register: shaft 7, owner M. Marwa, "props to be replaced — unsafe", written three weeks ago and never signed off.
Shaft register: a fatality in shaft 7 three years ago, J. Wambura, Robi's husband.
Records, Robi's line: shafts zone 05:35–06:30; washing ponds zone 06:35–07:10; shafts zone again 07:18–07:35.
In Robi's ore sack: a round pounding stone, washed, with red clay in a crack.
Chacha: Mwikwabe was at shaft 12 across the field with his crew from 05:30 until the shouting at 07:30.
Peter Magige: Jairus was buying at the Migori town gold market from 05:30. "He's always first."
Autopsy: one blow to the head from a heavy rounded stone, before death.
Autopsy: no soil or dust in the airways. She was not breathing when the earth fell on her.
Autopsy: death between 05:45 and 07:00.
Dr. Chebii: the pounding stone is consistent with the wound.
Lab: the clay in the stone's crack is the dark red band found only at shaft 7's mouth.
Robi: "I was at the washing ponds from five o'clock."
Robi: "Rosebella was a thief. Weigh my reference weight on her scale."
Robi admits she met Rosebella beside shaft 7 at dawn with the reference weight and told her she'd tell the whole field.
Robi: "She laughed at me and at my husband. She was alive when I left. Then I went to the ponds."
Mwikwabe: "Shaft 7 was propped properly. It was inspected last week."
Mwikwabe: the props were rotten and he couldn't afford timber. Only one prop in shaft 7 was sound. "I knew that shaft could fall."
Jairus: "I was at the Migori market."
Jairus: "Everyone said her scale was light. Nobody could prove it."

interrogations.intro: Robi keeps washing ore while she talks, swirling the pan without looking down. "I was at the ponds from five o'clock. Weigh my reference weight on her scale."

topics.reply: Three years. He went down that shaft and they brought him up dead. And she weighed his gold light for six years before that.

interrogations.intro: Mwikwabe stands at the rim of shaft 7 with his hat in his hands. "Shaft 7 was propped properly. It was inspected last week."

topics.reply: I was at shaft 12 with my crew all morning. Ask Chacha.

interrogations.intro: Jairus weighs a speck of gold on his own scale at a Migori stall without looking up. "I buy honest. Ask anyone."

topics.reply: Everyone said her scale was light. Nobody could prove it. I was here from half past five. Peter will tell you; he sold to me first.

interrogations.intro: Boke climbs out of shaft 8 with a bucket on a rope. "I heard them. I thought it was the usual morning shouting."
Nyakerario runs a muddy finger down her log. "Robi came at twenty to seven. Out of breath. Then she went off again."

contradictions.reaction: She stops swirling the pan. "I went to show her the weight. I told her I'd tell the whole field. She laughed at me and at my husband. Then I went to the ponds."
"The props were rotten. I couldn't afford timber. I told the women to be careful. I didn't kill her, I killed nobody. But I knew that shaft could fall."
Robi puts the pan down in the mud. "She said nobody would believe a miner." She holds out her red hands, palms up, and says nothing more.

timeOfDeath.note: From the argument at 05:50 to the kiosk that never opened at 06:30. The autopsy allows 05:45–07:00.

proof.concludes: Rosebella was struck with a rounded stone and was already dead when the shaft fell on her: there is no dust in her airways. The collapse didn't kill her.
The argument at shaft 7 at 05:50 was with Robi, who was in the shafts zone until 06:30, not at the ponds from five. Rosebella's kiosk never opened at 06:30: she died between 05:50 and 06:30.
The rotten shaft only fell because its one sound prop was struck out. Robi left the ponds at 07:15 and was back in the shafts zone from 07:18 to 07:35.

The stone in her sack carries shaft 7's clay and matches the wound. The scale weighed 10% light for years, including every gram her husband sold. Robi Wambura struck Rosebella with an ore-pounding stone, pushed her into the shaft and made it collapse.

reconstruction.text: For twelve years Rosebella weighs Macalder's gold on a scale with a magnet glued under its pan. Every reading is about 10% light. Robi's husband sells to her for six years, until shaft 7 kills him.
A schoolteacher gives Robi a certified 1-gram weight. On Monday she weighs it on Rosebella's scale: 0.90 g.

Tuesday, 05:50. Before the kiosk opens, Robi meets Rosebella beside shaft 7 with the weight in her hand. Rosebella laughs and says nobody will believe a miner. Robi strikes her with a pounding stone and pushes her into the shaft.
At 06:40 she arrives at the ponds, out of breath. At 07:15 she leaves her pan. At about 07:25, back at shaft 7, she knocks out the one sound prop.
07:30. The rotten props give way and the earth falls. At 09:00 the miners dig out the buyer whose kiosk never opened.

clockPlan.note: Two stamps: records on Robi's line, then a warrant on her shelter. The clay test (8 h) breaks her second story. No detention needed.
